title: Constant-coefficient balancing and its natural inverse-image chain map
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes and $\varphi:A\to B$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings. For $Z=X,Y$ use the constant coefficient sheaves $A_Z,B_Z$ and module categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the exact identified-coefficient inverse images $f_R^*$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the constant-section ring identifications $c_R:f^{-1}R_Y\simeq R_X$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Let $a_Z:A_Z\to B_Z$ be induced by $\varphi$ and let $r_Z$ be scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $a_Xc_A=c_Bf^{-1}a_Y$. The ordinary restriction comparison $\beta_N:r_Xf_B^*N\simeq f_A^*r_YN$, for a $B_Y$-module sheaf $N$, is the identity on the underlying inverse-image sheaf with its transported $A_X$-action.

There is a unique natural family of $A_X$-linear sheaf isomorphisms
$$t_M:f_A^*r_Y(M\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}r_X(f_A^*M\otimes_{A_X}B_X)$$
for $A_Y$-module sheaves $M$, whose value on the inverse-image unit section of $x\otimes s$ is $f^{-1}x\otimes c_B(f^{-1}s)$ over $X\times_YV$ for every $V\in Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $x\in M(V)$ and $s\in B_Y(V)$. Tensor products here are sheafified [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the formula concerns the images of presheaf pure tensors. The composite $t_M\circ\beta_{M\otimes B_Y}$ is $B_X$-linear. Thus the displayed comparison respects the $B_X$-action transported through $\beta$, as well as $A_X$-balancing.

For every possibly unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $A_Y$-module sheaves, the components $t_{P^i}$ and their inverses are chain maps, giving a natural chain isomorphism $t_P$ with these components [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In particular
$$(f_A^*d_P^i\otimes1)t_{P^i}=t_{P^{i+1}}f_A^*(d_P^i\otimes1).$$
With $B_Y[0]$ concentrated in degree zero, this is also the total-tensor comparison: its degree $i$ contains only $P^i\otimes B_Y$. No flatness, K-flatness or torsion hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 03EL, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback: bilinear adjunction construction, specialized to constant coefficients; coefficient-action and chain normalization of returned proof Steps 1–3

proof.text: Write $L=f^{-1}$ and $u(V)=X\times_YV$. The adjuncts of $a_Xc_A$ and $c_BL(a_Y)$ are $f_*(a_X)\rho_A$ and $\rho_Ba_Y$, by naturality of the inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. On each constant section $a\in A$ both give the constant section $\varphi(a)$ over $u(V)$, by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. These maps agree on all of $A_Y$: use the constant-preserving identification with the sheafification of the constant presheaf, and uniqueness in its sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Injectivity of adjunction gives $a_Xc_A=c_BL(a_Y)$. This argument uses equality of constant sections, never their distinctness, so also applies on the empty site.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text: In the identified-coefficient presentation of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the underlying abelian sheaf of $f_R^*N$ is $LN$, and an $r\in R_X$ acts through $c_R^{-1}(r)$ on $LN$. For a $B_Y$-module $N$, the action of $a\in A_X$ on $r_Xf_B^*N$ is therefore through $c_B^{-1}a_X(a)$, whereas that on $f_A^*r_YN$ is through $L(a_Y)c_A^{-1}(a)$. Step 1 makes these ring maps equal. The identity on $LN$ is consequently an $A_X$-linear isomorphism $\beta_N$, natural in $N$. Restriction changes neither additive sheaves nor their maps [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text: The finite-product action construction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] presents the geometric inverse image $L$ as an algebraic inverse image $I_A$ with coefficient ring $A_X$ in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]: the underlying identifications are the action-transport isomorphisms and $c_A$. The geometric adjunction and finite-limit preservation are supplied by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], on the compatible small sites already fixed there. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to $M$ and $r_YB_Y$. The map $c_B$ identifies $I_A(r_YB_Y)$ with $r_XB_X$ as $A_X$-modules by Step 1. Composing the resulting natural tensor isomorphism with $1\otimes c_B$ gives the required $A_X$-linear $t_M$. Its generalized pure-pairing equation gives the asserted formula on unit sections, because the inverse-image unit preserves products. More generally, apply that equation to the two projections from the test sheaf $|M|\times|B_Y|$ and its pure-pairing map. Since $L$ preserves products, it identifies the entire transported pairing, for arbitrary local sections of $LM$ and $LB_Y$, with the target pure pairing. Inverting $t_M$ gives the reverse pairing identity as well. Thus balancing is respected for sheafified tensors, without asserting that the tensor sheaf has only pure sections.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text: For uniqueness fix $M$ and put $S_M=f_A^*M\otimes_{A_X}B_X$. By the module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], an $A_X$-linear map $f_A^*r_Y(M\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)\to r_XS_M$ is determined by its adjunct $r_Y(M\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)\to f_{*,A}r_XS_M$. Direct image is evaluated over $u(V)$ and the adjunct is evaluated on inverse-image unit sections [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The required formula therefore fixes its values on every sheafified pure tensor $x\otimes s$ over every $V$. The injectivity part of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes the adjunct unique. Hence $t_M$ is unique, and its naturality also follows by applying this uniqueness to the two maps associated to a morphism $M\to M'$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text:
Put $H=f_B^*(M\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)$, $S=f_A^*M\otimes_{A_X}B_X$, and $g=t_M\beta_{M\otimes B_Y}:r_XH\to r_XS$. For local sections $m$ of $f_A^*M$ and $s,b$ of $B_X$, the pairing identity in Step 3 identifies $g^{-1}(m\otimes s)$ with the transported source pure tensor. In the source, multiplication on the coefficient factor satisfies $(x\otimes s')b'=x\otimes(s'b')$. Apply $L$ to this equality of sheaf maps on $|M|\times|B_Y|\times|B_Y|$. The finite-product comparison and the ring/module graph conditions of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] preserve multiplication and the $B$-action; $c_B$ preserves the ring multiplication, and $\beta$ is the identity on the underlying sheaf. The entire pairing identity from [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] therefore gives
$$g\bigl(g^{-1}(m\otimes s)b\bigr)=m\otimes(sb).$$
Here $m,s,b$ are arbitrary sections on $X$, not just unit images of sections on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text: The two pairings $(v,b)\mapsto g(g^{-1}(v)b)$ and $(v,b)\mapsto vb$ from $r_XS\times r_XB_X$ to $r_XS$ are $A_X$-bilinear: $g,g^{-1}$ are $A_X$-linear, and the $B_X$-module axioms together with restriction along $a_X$ give separate $A_X$-linearity. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] they define $A_X$-linear maps $(f_A^*M\otimes_{A_X}r_XB_X)\otimes_{A_X}r_XB_X\to r_XS$. Step 5 says that both send $(m\otimes s)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes sb$. The injectivity assertion of [lem-pd-sheaf-trilinear-universal] makes these maps equal. The original pairings are then equal by the same bilinear universal property. Taking $v=g(h)$ proves $g(hb)=g(h)b$ for every local section $h$ of $H$ and $b$ of $B_X$. This proves the asserted $B_X$-linearity; its inverse is $B_X$-linear by substituting $h=g^{-1}(v)$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text:
Apply the naturality of $t$ from Steps 3–4 to the module map $d_P^i:P^i\to P^{i+1}$. It gives exactly
$$(f_A^*d_P^i\otimes1)t_{P^i}=t_{P^{i+1}}f_A^*(d_P^i\otimes1).$$
The functors in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] act termwise, and the tensor differential with a degree-zero coefficient is $d_P^i\otimes1$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus these components define a chain map. Multiplying the displayed equation on the left by $t_{P^{i+1}}^{-1}$ and on the right by $t_{P^i}^{-1}$ gives the chain equation for the inverse components. Their composites are the identity in each degree, so $t_P$ is a chain isomorphism. Applying naturality to every component of a chain morphism $P\to Q$ proves naturality in complexes. The argument treats each $i$ separately and requires no bound on $P$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient specialization and explicit normalization of its bilinear construction

proof.text: In the total tensor construction of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the only nonzero summand in total degree $i$ for $P\otimes B_Y[0]$ has bidegree $(i,0)$. The second differential is zero, including its sign $(-1)^i$, and the first is $d_P^i\otimes1$. Hence Step 7 is precisely the total-tensor comparison and its inverse. The construction used only ordinary tensor isomorphisms, coefficient ring identifications and naturality; no preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by scalar extension was invoked, so no flatness, K-flatness or torsion hypothesis is needed.
